messages:
Alex (cust-app): Hey team — we've got a production issue where websocket streaming responses are getting truncated mid-token. Client sees a final empty chunk and the UI stalls. Started ~2026-03-15. Request ID: req_01Gx8Y2Z9aA3tQ. Using our Electron app (Node 18 + ws v8). Happens on Chrome/Win and macOS.

Sasha (support): Sorry to hear that — we'll take a look. Can you paste the minimal repro steps, the exact request ID(s), and a short wscat/curl equivalent you used? Also include SDK version, auth token scope, and whether this is always reproducible or intermittent.

Alex (cust-app): Repro is fairly frequent (~1/20 streams). Full details: SDK: custom websocket client (ws@8.13.0). Auth: bearer token (app:read,chat:write). Here's how we connect via wscat for a quick test (replace <REDACTED_TOKEN>):

```
# wscat example
wscat -c "wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-redwood-1&stream=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>"
```

When reproducing with wscat we sometimes see the last chunk arrive as `\"\"` (empty string) then the socket stays open but no more data. Client logs show repeated 0-byte messages in the buffer. Request ID above corresponds to one of those runs.

Devon (eng-oncall): Can you dump the raw websocket frames (binary/utf8) and paste a short excerpt? Also include the server-side request id and the trace id if present (we look for trace= in logs). If you can run `curl` to hit the non-streaming endpoint we can compare response completeness.

Alex (cust-app): Pasted a small frame dump from our capture:

```
[2026-03-15T18:21:02.312Z] FRAME (text): {"id":"msg-1","delta":"Hello, wo"
[2026-03-15T18:21:02.328Z] FRAME (text): {"id":"msg-1","delta":"rld!\n"}
[2026-03-15T18:21:02.329Z] FRAME (text): {"id":"msg-1","delta":""}   <-- empty delta
[2026-03-15T18:21:02.330Z] (no more frames for ~8s)
```

We can also reproduce by hitting the SSE endpoint from a node script, which shows the same empty event payload occasionally. Sample node SSE client we used: 

```
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sse?model=gpt-redwood-1', {
  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>' }
});
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('MSG', e.data);
```

Maya (support-escalations): Thanks — please upload a debug bundle with: client logs, the raw frame capture (text), a HAR (if browser), and a pcap (if possible). Use our secure upload URL: https://files.redwood.ai/safe-upload (choose "support_debug"). When you upload include a short manifest.txt with the request ID and the timestamp window. Mark tokens as REDACTED in any artifacts. :lock:  

ingest-bot: Debug bundle requested: req=1779991111, job=collect-debug-178, status=pending

Devon (eng-oncall): While you gather that, we'll check edge proxies (nginx/gateway) for chunking settings and idle timeouts. Two hypotheses: 1) upstream buffer flush producing empty event frames, or 2) client socket library treating a zero-length payload as a keepalive and then failing to resume assembly. We'll run a server-side trace for req_01Gx8Y2Z9aA3tQ and report back.

Alex (cust-app): Uploading now — bundle name `alex-app-debug-req_01Gx8Y2Z9.zip`. Included pcap and node frame dump. I redacted all tokens. Link: s3://private-support-uploads/alex/alex-app-debug-req_01Gx8Y2Z9.zip (will set permissions to support team).

Sasha (support): Got it, thanks. Devon — can you prioritize the trace and check the runtime logs around 2026-03-15T18:21:00Z to 18:21:10Z for that req id? Alex — we'll post next steps and any quick workarounds (client-side) after we confirm. For now, if you can add a client-side retry that reopens the stream on an empty final chunk that would be a useful mitigation. :+1:

Devon (eng-oncall): Confirmed I pulled trace trace_9a1f3e for req_01Gx8Y2Z9aA3tQ. Preliminary note: gateway sent three 0-length frames during the stream. Looking at worker logs now to see if model actor emitted an empty delta or if the gateway wrapped an internal flush. Will update in ~30m.

Alex (cust-app): Thanks everyone. I'll keep monitoring and will test a client-side retry patch. Please ping me if you need any more artifacts.

Maya (support-escalations): Appreciate the fast turnaround. We'll keep this thread for updates. If we need to escalate to infra for gateway tuning I'll loop them in. :telephone_receiver:
